title: College Board confirms data breach after unauthorized password changes
content_md: College Board has confirmed it suffered a data breach after students reported unexpected password changes on Thanksgiving, and the organization said threat actors gained access to its account registration and financial aid application systems. College Board is a nonprofit organization that provides college admissions and financial aid services to millions of students. The organization creates and administers the SAT and Advanced Placement (AP) exams, provides students with access to their exam scores, and operates the CSS Profile and Institutional Documentation Service (IDOC), which colleges and universities use to evaluate students' eligibility for financial aid. In a security incident update published Friday, College Board confirmed that threat actors gained access to systems used to create new accounts and submit CSS Profile applications for financial aid. "Our preliminary assessment is that this activity involved sophisticated AI tools that have recently been leveraged to gain access to the systems of other major institutions worldwide," reads College Board's security update . "While our investigation is ongoing, we have determined that the activity involved access to the systems students and professionals use to create new College Board accounts and to submit CSS Profile applications for financial aid."
